plan_recap.q1_signal_path: The block frame (x 22.95-51.5, y 32.95-78.0) holds the MCU cluster; every wiped net must get from its pads back to the block-edge ports on dR. Power runs on the inner planes, the buses go as groups, control links go short and direct. 98 anchored pieces already draw exactly that.
plan_recap.q2_what_blocks: Nothing physical and nothing on the drawing side. What blocks is the router way of deciding: it routes each edge independently and in order, so whoever is served last starves (the residual rotates). Every attempt to PRE-ASSIGN the answer (whole-net band, layered y-bands, per-corridor slots) is expressed through the one knob the maze has - the solve domain - and a hard domain can only forbid, never prefer. That is why the last attempt turned 2 residuals into 47.
plan_recap.q3_human_plan: A human layout engineer would not fence each net into a 0.4 mm strip. They would route the whole bundle, then fix only the collisions: rip up the conflicting runs and re-route them with a penalty for reusing occupied space, repeating a bounded number of times until nothing conflicts. In plain words: let everyone draw first, then settle the arguments, instead of handing out lanes that nobody can reach.
